name: hat.sh
tagline: Encrypt and decrypt files in this tab. Nothing leaves this device.
description:
Drop a file, pick a password (or a pair of keys), and get an encrypted copy back — or drop a .enc and get the original back. The file never goes anywhere. There is no account, no upload, and nothing is sent off this device.

An unofficial port of hat.sh by sh-dv. Same file format: a file this app encrypts opens in hat.sh, and a file hat.sh encrypted opens here. You can lock it with a password, or with a key pair if you would rather exchange keys than share a password.

Very large files have to fit in this tab at once, the same way hat.sh already does in Safari. A few hundred megabytes is fine; a multi-gigabyte file may not fit. Old hat.sh v1 files (the “Encrypted Using Hat.sh” header) are refused rather than guessed at. Passwords must be at least 12 characters.

Nothing is fetched, and nothing you drop in is sent anywhere.
